The accurate statement is: law as a medium means formal, general rules that steer the state and the economy; law as an institution means lifeworld-based shared norms and values that still need moral-practical justification. Law as a medium is positivized steering law whose legitimacy comes from the legal order as a whole, while law as an institution gives binding form to communicative expectations such as constitutional basics and the moral core of criminal law. The alternative that treats “medium” as mass-media presentation and “institution” as the courts misses Habermas’s distinction.

CONFIDENCE: 90
